body:
Leah (Support): FYI customer reported a 403 when they try to export project audit logs via API after we rolled org alias normalization last night. They say this only affects API keys issued before the migration.

Diego (Eng): Can you paste the error response and the curl they used?

Leah (Support): Sent by customer: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/acc-123/export/audit"`
Response: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden` body: `{"error":"permission_denied","message":"You do not have permission to export audit logs for project acc-123"}`
They also said UI export works for their admin user, but not with the service API key used by their CI pipeline.

Ava (SRE): Do we have the request id or the token fingerprint? Ask them for `x-request-id` from headers, and whether the API key is a project-scoped key or org-scoped.

Leah (Support): Customer returned `x-request-id: rq_01G9ZQ9FJA2` and says key was created in org `acme-old` pre-migration; project now has alias `acc-123` and lives under org `acme-new`. Key metadata they provided: `scope: ["project:read", "project:export"]`, `created_by: service-account-42`, `created_at: 2023-11-02T15:12:00Z`

Diego (Eng): Huh. We enacted alias normalization which canonicalizes org IDs; old pre-migration API keys should have been remapped but maybe not for some keys tied to service-account roles. Possible mismatch: token still binds to old org ID string and our authZ lookup uses normalized alias. 

Ava (SRE): On authZ path, we first map token -> principal -> org_id via `token.org` claim. If that claim equals `acme-old` but project record uses `acme-new`, the project-level check `principal.has_role(project, export)` will fail with 403.

Leah (Support): Customer asked if this is a regression from last night's deploy. They need a fast workaround — CI is blocked.

Diego (Eng): Short-term workaround: re-issue a new API key scoped to the project (preferred). Longer-term: run a targeted role remap for service-account-42 tokens where `created_at < 2024-05-01` and `org_alias` in the old alias table. I'll prepare a safe remap script.

Ava (SRE): While Diego readies the script, we can also allow a temporary fallback that accepts `legacy_org_alias` from a special header for export endpoints: `X-Redwood-Legacy-Org: acme-old`. That will let CI run while we fix tokens. Need product signoff but we can enable it for 30 minutes for this customer only.

Leah (Support): Customer prefers re-issue but said CI automation is slow to accept manual rotation. They asked if we can programmatically rotate their key and push to their pipeline.

Diego (Eng): We can. I need the service-account ID and project ID. Leah, confirm we have the customer's consent to rotate keys on their behalf. Also include the pipeline secret path so we can push the new key.

Leah (Support): Customer gave OK and provided `vault:path/acme/ci/api-key`.

role-sync-bot: role-sync started for org `acme-old` -> `acme-new` (task id: sync_2025_04_01_01).

Ava (SRE): Diego, I'll run the remap in dry-run first against a dev copy. Expected steps: 1) list tokens for service-account-42 created before cutoff, 2) map `org_alias` via alias table, 3) update token principal mapping, 4) re-evaluate effective roles. Dry-run will log which tokens flip to the new org id.

Diego (Eng): Sounds good. Add a changelog entry and create a canary that only touches tokens for customers who explicitly consented (like this one).

Leah (Support): I'll tell the customer: short-term we can rotate their key into Vault and update pipeline; medium-term we'll run a consented remap; we can also enable the temporary header fallback if they want immediate unblock without rotating.

Leah (Support): Customer accepted automated rotation for now and asked for ETA.

Ava (SRE): I can run the dry-run in ~20m and then a targeted remap for their tokens in ~45m, followed by verification of the export endpoint using the new key.

Diego (Eng): I'll prepare the key-rotation automation: generate new key, scope it to `project:export`, push to `vault:path/acme/ci/api-key:new`, and mark old key revoked. Post the command here once ready.

role-sync-bot: dry-run log uploaded: https://internal.redwood.s3/role-sync/sync_2025_04_01_01/dryrun.log

Leah (Support): Customer confirmed they see the new key in their vault after Diego's script ran. They tried the same curl and export succeeded: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` stream starts.

Diego (Eng): Great. I'll schedule a safe remap for tokens created before migration for consenting customers. We'll add an audit event `org_alias_remap` and notify customers.

Ava (SRE): Postmortem notes: root cause = alias canonicalization changed the canonical org id used during authz checks; tokens with pre-migration principal mapping to the deprecated alias were not auto-forwarded to the normalized alias in one remap edge-case (service-account-created tokens). Remediation = targeted remap + better migration tests.

Leah (Support): Marking this resolved for the customer. Will follow up with email + rotation summary. :white_check_mark:

Diego (Eng): Filed follow-up ticket ENG-3289 to add a migration test and a one-off remap tool.

Ava (SRE): Leaving monitoring watch on similar 403 spikes for next 6 hours.

Leah (Support): Closing thread once SRE confirms no other affected orgs.
